skill.name: developer-experience
skill.description: Developer Experience specialist for project setup, onboarding, workflow automation, tooling configuration, and developer productivity improvements.

security_audit.summary: AI review found the static alerts to be false positives caused by Markdown examples, local setup snippets, and onboarding placeholders. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, hidden execution, or malicious persistence in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Onboarding placeholder {{SYSTEM}} can be misread by scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Rename the placeholder to {{SERVICE_NAME}} or {{INTERNAL_PLATFORM}} to avoid prompt-related ambiguity.

remediation.issue: Shell examples include commands that users may copy directly.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note that generated setup scripts and cleanup commands should be reviewed before execution.

remediation.issue: Shell rc alias guidance references persistent user configuration files.
remediation.suggestion: Mark aliases as optional and recommend project-local documentation before changing user shell startup files.

content.value_statement: Project setup and daily workflows can slow teams with repeated manual steps. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design setup guides, scripts, shortcuts, and tooling improvements.
actual_capabilities: Reviews project setup steps and suggests faster onboarding flows.
Drafts setup scripts, package scripts, Makefile targets, and shell aliases.
Creates onboarding guide structures with prerequisites, workflows, and troubleshooting sections.
Suggests IDE settings, linting, formatting, and git hook improvements.
Defines developer experience metrics such as time to first success and manual steps.
Documents recurring development tasks and recommended automation points.
limitations: It does not execute or validate generated scripts by itself.
Generated commands should be reviewed before use in production repositories.
Examples focus on common JavaScript and shell workflows.
It needs project context to make accurate recommendations.

use_cases.title: Create a New Project Setup Flow
use_cases.description: Design setup steps, validation checks, and first-run commands for a new repository.

use_cases.title: Reduce Team Workflow Friction
use_cases.description: Identify repeated manual tasks and convert them into documented scripts or shortcuts.

use_cases.title: Improve New Developer Onboarding
use_cases.description: Build a practical onboarding guide with prerequisites, key files, workflows, and troubleshooting.

prompt_templates.title: Find Quick Improvements
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a repository workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository and list the top five developer workflow improvements. Focus on setup, testing, linting, and daily commands.

prompt_templates.title: Create Onboarding Guide
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a new developer onboarding document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an onboarding guide for a new developer joining this project. Include prerequisites, setup steps, key files, workflows, and troubleshooting.

prompt_templates.title: Design Automation
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert repeated tasks into safe automation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design npm scripts, Makefile targets, and git hooks for common development tasks. Explain each command, expected benefit, and review risk.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Developer Experience
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the developer experience for this project. Prioritize improvements by impact, estimate effort, and propose a staged implementation plan.

output_examples.output: A prioritized improvement list covering missing validation, unclear prerequisites, slow first run, and recommended setup documentation.

output_examples.input: Create onboarding material for a new developer.
output_examples.output: A structured guide with quick links, day-one setup, codebase orientation, common tasks, troubleshooting, and completion checks.

output_examples.input: Suggest shortcuts for daily development work.
output_examples.output: A set of named task recommendations for development, testing, linting, formatting, database setup, and cleanup with brief explanations.

best_practices: Provide the repository structure and current setup instructions before asking for improvements.
Review generated shell commands before running them or adding them to automation.
Measure outcomes with onboarding time, manual step count, and feedback loop duration.
anti_patterns: Do not add automation that hides important security or deployment decisions.
Do not copy generated shell scripts into production workflows without review.
Do not optimize tooling before understanding the team workflow and project constraints.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps improve project setup, onboarding, development scripts, IDE configuration, git hooks, and workflow documentation.

faq.question: Can it run setup scripts for me?
faq.answer: No. It can draft and explain scripts, but users should review and run commands themselves.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it only for JavaScript projects?
faq.answer: No, but its examples emphasize npm, shell scripts, Makefiles, VS Code, and common web development tooling.

faq.question: How should teams use the recommendations?
faq.answer: Treat them as a review plan, then test changes in a branch before sharing them with the team.

faq.question: Does it replace developer documentation?
faq.answer: No. It helps draft and improve documentation, but maintainers must verify project-specific details.
